frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of THE HIND/REAR — the back-side, or that which lies behind / comes after (spatially, sequentially, or temporally): the rear as a locus (a body's back, a garment's back, the hindmost tail-end of a group), the direction "toward the rear/backward," and by extension the "back-end / after / outcome" of an event or matter. Every occurrence names, faces toward, moves toward, arrives at, or attends to this rear/after pole.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of THE HIND/REAR — the back-side, or that which lies behind / comes after (spatially, sequentially, or temporally): the rear as a locus (a body's back, a garment's back, the hindmost tail-end of a group), the direction "toward the rear/backward," and by extension the "back-end / after / outcome" of an event or matter. Every occurrence names, faces toward, moves toward, arrives at, or attends to this rear/after pole.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Six form/sense families all resolve to a single "rear / behind / after" residue. (A) Anatomical/physical rear (form N, dubur/adbaar): the shirt torn "min dubur" = from the back (12:25:6:1, 12:27:6:1, 12:28:6:1); striking "their faces and their backs" (8:50:10:2, 47:27:7:2); "he turns his back / they turn the backs" in flight (8:16:4:1 dubura-hu, 54:45:4:2 al-dubur, 3:111:8:2, 8:15:11:2, 33:15:9:2, 48:22:6:2, 59:12:13:2 al-adbaar); "reverting upon their backs" = going backward (17:46:18:1, 47:25:5:1, 5:21:12:1, 4:47:18:1); "follow behind their rears" (15:65:7:1). Here the residue is fully surface-visible: dubur = the back. (B) Hindmost extremity / tail-end (form N, daabir): "the daabir of the wrongdoing people was cut off" = the very last/rearmost trace extirpated (6:45:2:1, 7:72:7:1, 8:7:22:1, 15:66:6:1); daabir = "that which comes hindmost." (C) Temporal after/going-behind: "the adbaar (aftermaths/ends) of prostration" (50:40:4:2) and "the idbaar (going-behind/setting) of the stars" (52:49:4:2) — the rear applied to time: the after-part of an act, the receding of the stars behind the horizon. (D) Form IV adbara / participle mudbir = to present the back, hence recede/turn away: "then he turned his back" (74:23:2:1, 79:22:2:1, 70:17:3:1), "the night when it retreats/turns its back" (74:33:3:1), and the mudbir cluster "they turned away, backs-turned" (21:57:7:1, 27:10:9:1, 27:80:11:1, 28:31:10:1, 30:52:11:1, 37:90:3:1, 40:33:3:1, 9:25:23:1). Here the root supplies the "rear/back," and Form IV supplies "give/show the back" → recede. (E) Form II dabbara / participle mudabbiraat = to attend to the back-ends/outcomes of a matter, i.e. dispose/manage it: "He directs the affair" (10:3:15:1, 10:31:21:1, 13:2:19:1, 32:5:1:1) and "those managing the affair" (79:5:1:3). The residue "the after/outcome of the amr" is reached through the internally-attested "rear=after/end" bridge (see families B and C). (F) Form V tadabbara = to make oneself examine the back-ends/consequences of discourse → ponder deeply: "do they not reflect on the Qur'an / the saying / its verses" (4:82:2:1, 47:24:2:1, 23:68:2:1, 38:29:5:2) — the reflexive of family E's "attend to what lies behind/after the words."
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions to isolate the residue: (a) FORM — N gives the rear as a static locus (dubur/adbaar) or hindmost extremity (daabir) or verbal-noun after-time (idbaar/adbaar); Form IV (adbara/mudbir) adds the denominal/causative act "present the back" → recede; Form II (dabbara/mudabbir) adds "dispose the back-ends/outcomes" → manage; Form V (tadabbara) adds the reflexive-intensive "examine the after/behind of X" → ponder. (b) CONSTRUCTION — "min dubur" (source: from the rear), "walla/radda ... al-adbaar / 'alaa adbaari-him" (turning-motion vectored to the rear; the turning is supplied by wly/rdd, not dbr), "qutti'a/yaqta'u daabir + genitive" (the cutting is supplied by qT', dbr only names the tail-end cut), "adbaar/idbaar + genitive of an event" (temporal aftermath), "dabbara/tadabbara + al-amr/al-qur'aan/al-qawl" (object whose back-ends are disposed or examined). (c) PARTICIPANTS — God (manager of the affair), humans (fleers, ponderers, the extirpated), night/stars (receders); none of these alter the residue. (d) CONTEXT — military rout, eschatological punishment, cosmological order, revelation-reflection, Joseph narrative. After removing all four layers, the constant remainder is "the hind/rear — back-side, or what lies behind/comes after."
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The Form II "manage/direct the affair" cluster — "yudabbiru l-amr" (10:3:15:1, 10:31:21:1, 13:2:19:1, 32:5:1:1) and "al-mudabbiraat amran" (79:5:1:3) — is the single hardest case, because on the surface "govern/direct" shows no visible "back." It reconciles through a bridge that is itself internally attested, not imported from outside: the same data independently establish "rear = tail-end/after/outcome" (daabir = the hindmost trace cut off, 6:45/7:72/8:7/15:66; adbaar al-sujood = the after of prostration, 50:40; idbaar al-nujoom = the stars going behind, 52:49). Reading dabbara as "to attend to and set the back-ends/outcomes of the affair" therefore recovers the residue from within the packet. The reconciliation is genuine but requires conceptual extension, so it does not count as a clean surface presence.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is "turning away / directional recession from the rear" (motion-centered rather than locus-centered). It fits families D, and the flight verses, but internal evidence arbitrates against it as the ROOT contribution: (1) the anatomical statives have no motion — a shirt "torn from the back" (12:25) and blows on "their backs" (8:50, 47:27) are pure rear-locus, no turning; (2) in "yuwalloona l-adbaar" the turning is carried by the separate root wly while dbr supplies the object "the backs" — so dbr is the rear that gets turned, not the turning itself; (3) adbara is morphologically Form IV (denominal "give/show the back"), which presupposes a prior noun "back." Hence "the rear/back-side" is more basic and "turning-away" is a form-plus-construction actualization of it. A second alternative, "management/order," fails immediately because it cannot cover the ~34 anatomical/directional/tail-end/temporal occurrences.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) قبل/qbl — the polar opposite "front/before/facing" (qubul vs dubur); dbr is exclusively the REAR/after pole, never the front. (2) خلف/xlf — "behind/succession/successor"; xlf foregrounds one thing coming-after-and-replacing another (dynastic/successional), whereas dbr foregrounds the rear-side as a physical/positional locus and the tail-end/consequence. (3) ولّى/wly — pure turning/orientation; the frequent pairing "yuwalloona l-adbaar" shows the two roots are complementary, wly=turn, dbr=the back turned. (4) عقب/Ʒqb — heel / immediate following-trace / consequence; overlaps at "aftermath" but Ʒqb is the heel/next-step, dbr the whole rear/hindmost. Falsifiability: the hypothesis fails if any confirmed dbr occurrence required a "front/before/facing" sense, or a pure turning with no rear reference, or a dabbara/tadabbara reading that could NOT be construed as attending-to / examining-the back-ends/outcomes of something.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — "the hind/rear: back-side, or what lies behind/comes after" — is recoverable in all 44 occurrences with a determinate directional pole (rear, sharply opposed to قبل=front) and clear distinctness from wly/xlf/Ʒqb. For roughly 34 occurrences (families A anatomical, B hindmost tail-end, C temporal after, D Form IV recede/turn-back) the residue is surface-visible and needs no inference. The strength is held to MODERATE, not STRONG, solely because the 8-9 Form II/V occurrences ("direct the affair," "ponder the Qur'an": 10:3, 10:31, 13:2, 32:5, 79:5, 4:82, 47:24, 23:68, 38:29) recover the residue only through a metaphorical bridge (rear → back-end/outcome → dispose/examine what comes after). Critically, that bridge is licensed from WITHIN the same packet (daabir = tail-end; adbaar al-sujood = aftermath; idbaar al-nujoom = going-behind establish "rear=after/end"), so it is a reconciled internally-attested extension rather than forcing — meeting the PREFERRED bar. No occurrence is contradicted or absent; inconsistent_refs is empty. The residual inference in the II/V families is what separates this from a fully surface-recoverable STRONG verdict.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Refutation attempt: The spatial/physical core (families A-D, ~35 of 44) is surface-visible and unassailable — dubur (posterior: 12:25/27/28, shirt torn from the back), adbar (backs turned in flight/retreat: 8:16, 54:45, 3:111, 8:15, 33:15, 48:22, 59:12; struck backs 8:50, 47:27; reverting on backs 17:46, 47:25, 5:21, 4:47; follow the rears 15:65), dabir (hindmost trace extirpated: 6:45, 7:72, 8:7, 15:66), temporal after (adbar al-sujud 50:40, idbar al-nujum 52:49), and Form IV recede/show-the-back (74:23, 79:22, 70:17, 74:33 + mudbir cluster 21:57, 27:10, 27:80, 28:31, 30:52, 37:90, 40:33, 9:25). No failure there.

Hardest cases = the 9 Form II (dabbara al-amr = He directs/manages the affair: 10:3, 10:31, 13:2, 32:5; N(II) mudabbirat 79:5) and Form V (tadabbara = ponder: 4:82, 47:24, 23:68, 38:29). In these the occurrence does NOT name, face, or move toward any rear/back — the "hind/rear" is absent from the surface. The candidate reaches them only through the abstraction "attend to the back-ends/outcomes of a matter," which turns its headline clause ("attends to this rear/after pole") into a near-unfalsifiable catch-all for any purposive/reflective verb (managing anything = attending to its outcome; pondering = considering what lies behind words). This is a genuine over-breadth / underdetermined-core problem at the derived pole, and it collapses semantically onto the outcome sense of the neighbor root.

Resolution / why not REFUTED: the bridge is monogenetic and classically standard (tadbir/tadabbur derive from النظر في أدبار/عواقب الأمور) and is internally corroborated by dabir (hindmost) and adbar al-sujud (after), so this is NOT homonymy or a true semantic split, and not purely ad-hoc. Hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rather than REFUTED.

Neighbor-root contrast: distinctiveness holds for the CORE because dbr's signature markers — dubur (bodily posterior), idbar (showing-the-back/retreat), dabir (hindmost remnant) — are not shared by khlf (generic positional behind / succession / replacement), ʿqb (heel / immediate following of footsteps / ʿaqiba=consequence), or wr' (behind). BUT the derived "outcome/manage" residue of Form II/V blurs directly into ʿqb's ʿaqiba (outcome/consequence), which is precisely why those 9 are flagged: at that pole the contribution is no longer discriminating. distinctiveness_ok=true is judged on the core signature; falsifiable=true because a clear failure condition exists (an occurrence with no back/behind/after/outcome sense) — the Form II/V set presses against it but does not fully break the monogenetic chain.
